summary: plan worker startup and import preload
pull_request_body: This change adds a session-scoped fixture in tests/conftest.py that imports the heavy modules (pydantic_ai, anthropic, kubernetes, textual) once per xdist worker. It removes the first-import cost from individual test durations. The full suite on 16 workers takes 287 s, but the tests account for only 151 s. The other 136 s is worker startup, repeated collection, and first-import costs. This fixture targets the import cost, which the issue identifies as the largest share that a single code change can remove. The measurement numbers are reported in the PR description from three runs on an idle host.
why: The full test suite on 16 xdist workers takes 287 s, but the tests account for only 151 s. The other 136 s is worker startup, repeated collection, and first-import costs of heavy libraries. Each worker pays the import cost of pydantic_ai, anthropic, kubernetes, and textual in the test that first uses them. #2371 asks to measure this overhead and apply the change with the largest share.
what_changes: Add a session-scoped fixture in tests/conftest.py that imports pydantic_ai, anthropic, kubernetes, and textual before any test runs on a worker.
Add a test that verifies the session fixture pre-loads the heavy modules and that the fixture scope is session.
feasibility: The issue states 287 s total, 151 s tests, 136 s overhead, measured on 2026-10-27 on a 16-CPU host with 11,285 tests.
tests/test_cli_startup_imports.py exists and uses python -X importtime, confirming the measurement approach is already in the codebase.
CHANGELOG.md:1645 records that #1338 already deferred some heavy imports, so the remaining modules (pydantic_ai, anthropic, kubernetes, textual) are the target.
The CI config uses -n logical --dist worksteal (CHANGELOG.md:1197), confirming 16 workers on a 16-CPU host.
First check: uv run pytest tests/test_cli_startup_imports.py -v to confirm the import budget tests pass.
Second check: uv run pytest --collect-only -q | wc -l to confirm the test count is near 11,285.
Third check: uv run python -X importtime -c 'import pydantic_ai' to measure the import cost of the heaviest module.
existing_tool: pytest-xdist is in use for parallel execution. python -X importtime is built into CPython and already used by tests/test_cli_startup_imports.py. pytest --durations and -v with xdist provide per-test timing and worker attribution. No new tool is needed. The session fixture uses pytest's built-in fixture system.

decisions.decision: Use a session-scoped fixture in tests/conftest.py to pre-import heavy modules.
decisions.reason: This moves the import cost from individual tests to a known, one-time place per worker. It is the smallest change that removes the import overhead from test durations.

decisions.decision: Target pydantic_ai, anthropic, kubernetes, and textual as the heavy modules.
decisions.reason: These are listed in CONST_CLI_HEAVY_MODULES in tests/test_cli_startup_imports.py:17 and are the modules the issue identifies as the heaviest first imports.

decisions.decision: Use importlib.import_module instead of a bare import statement.
decisions.reason: A bare import at module level in conftest.py would run at collection time, not at session start. importlib.import_module inside the fixture body runs at session start, which is the intended timing.

rejected.alternative: Reduce the worker count to -n 3 or -n 2 on the 4-CPU runner.
rejected.evidence: This reduces parallelism and increases wall time. The issue lists it as a candidate but the session fixture targets the root cause (repeated imports) without reducing parallelism.

rejected.alternative: Remove imports from the top of test modules to shorten collection.
rejected.evidence: This is a large refactor across many test files. The session fixture achieves the same goal (removing import cost from tests) with a single change to conftest.py.

added.name: test-worker-import-preload
added.text: The test session SHALL import the heavy modules pydantic_ai, anthropic, kubernetes, and textual once per xdist worker via a session-scoped fixture, so that no test body carries the first-import cost of a heavy module.

scenarios.name: heavy modules present after session start
scenarios.when: the session-scoped fixture completes on a worker
scenarios.then: sys.modules contains pydantic_ai, anthropic, kubernetes, and textual before the first test executes

scenarios.name: fixture scope is session
scenarios.then: the scope parameter of the pytest.fixture decorator is 'session'

groups.title: Add session fixture for heavy module imports
groups.test: Write a test in tests/test_conftest_import_preload.py that asserts sys.modules contains pydantic_ai, anthropic, kubernetes, and textual after the session fixture runs, and that the fixture scope is 'session'
groups.implementation: Add a session-scoped fixture in tests/conftest.py that imports pydantic_ai, anthropic, kubernetes, and textual. Name it _preload_heavy_modules. Use pytest.fixture(scope='session'). Import each module with importlib.import_module to avoid static analysis issues
